annotations.subject: http://example.org/scholarly-metadata-ontology#Exploring_Teacher-Chatbot_Interaction_8dab0a
annotations.value: AI-based chatbots hold promise for accelerating learning in K-12 settings, yet careless design can produce counter-productive outcomes. This study examined middle-school teachers’ perspectives on large-language-model (LLM) chatbots integrated into a block-based programming environment. Eleven teacher teams participated in a professional-development workshop where they used a chatbot-enhanced activity. Qualitative analysis of audio transcripts and interaction logs yielded three teacher profiles-explorer, frustrated, and mixed-reflecting differing scaffolding needs. Teachers reported benefits such as improved prompting skills and self-confidence, alongside risks including reduced learning depth and critical-thinking. Design recommendations emphasize scaffolding chatbot introduction, enabling teacher control of chatbot features, and providing guidance on appropriate chatbot use. The findings inform human-centered chatbot design to support teachers and learners in middle-school coding activities.
